stories.Headline: AI Coding Agents Failed to Generate Valid Test Cases: 100% Overestimation of AI-Generated Code Pass Rate
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Nanjing University, led by Professor Liu Jiaheng, have found that AI coding agents write tests that look reliable under standard benchmarks but fail a stricter check. The team introduced TestPrism, a benchmark of 300 test tasks drawn from 17 sources, with 3000 candidate implementations. Under single reference evaluation, the strongest of 14 agent configurations passed 59.67 percent of tests against one reference answer. Under the stricter Joint Success Function, the same configuration reached only 28.00 percent. Each task in TestPrism is paired with a panel of one reference implementation, four correct alternative implementations and five wrong implementations.

A valid test must fail on the original code, accept every correct implementation and reject every wrong one. The tasks come from six languages, including Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, C/C++ and Go, and span 67 code repositories and projects. They are grouped into six categories, with Bug Fix containing 167 tasks, Programs and Algorithms 53, Performance Optimization 28, Feature Expansion 20, Project and Workflow 19, and Refactoring and Migration 13. The paper's authors are the team of Professor Liu Jiaheng at Nanjing University, who built the benchmark and proposed the new metric. The article says the team argues that existing benchmarks assume a single correct answer is enough to judge a test, an assumption they say is hardly valid.

Two experts with development experience independently reviewed task requirements and verifiers, and tasks still in doubt were excluded, with a Cohen's kappa of 0.68. The researchers also describe the Joint Success Function as the core indicator, noting that single reference evaluation is only its most lenient special case. Developers and teams that rely on generated tests for self-verification, code review and reinforcement learning rewards are affected, since the article says the quality of those tests determines whether downstream decisions can be trusted. The article says the study examined 286 failure traces, which the researchers categorized into three groups and seven error mechanisms. Other existing benchmarks, including TestGenEval, CLOVER, MultiFileTest, SWT Bench and TDD Bench Verified, were described as following a fail-to-pass criterion.

Works such as OmniCode and SWE Mutation were said to test rejection of wrong variants but not acceptance of correct alternatives. Background from the article: test generation evaluation has been an established problem, and Coding Agents such as Codex and Claude Code are already writing unit tests, reproduction cases and regression tests. The article states that the researchers proposed TestHelix, which uses heterogeneous synthesis, peer cross-validation and recursive self-improvement. Under the same reasoning budget, TestHelix raised JSF by 11.67 to 12.00 percentage points.

The panels were built from real agent solutions, not artificially injected defects, and were checked for diversity using AST distance and Jaccard measures. The article reports the results for 14 configurations across six model families, with the best configuration of each family shown in a table. It does not say how the new framework performs on other benchmarks, whether the 1,700 training tasks will be released, or how the results compare with human-written tests. More to follow.

Articles.Title: AI Coding Agents Failed to Generate Valid Test Cases: 100% Overestimation of AI-Generated Code Pass Rate - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Tens of Millions Yuan Investment, Only 1.8M Box Office: Why Did the First AI-Generated Theatrical Film Flop?
stories.Summary:
Sanxingdui: Future Past, the first domestic theatrical film produced with AI technology, was released in Chinese cinemas on October 23 and has since struggled badly at the box office. The film is produced by Boyue Xingji Lantu companies under Bona Film Group, with Shengshu Technology providing AI technical support. By November 11, its cumulative box office had reached 1.802 million yuan. On November 12, its 21st day of release, 29 screenings were scheduled at 17 Beijing cinemas, yet not a single ticket had been sold by noon. The film has drawn wide attention because of its production method rather than its commercial results.

The film runs about 100 minutes and is set against the ancient Shu civilization of Sanxingdui and a future world. Iconic relics such as the Bronze Divine Tree, the Great Bronze Standing Figure and the Bronze Vertical Eye Mask appear throughout the story. In the plot, future humans depend too heavily on algorithms and fall into a global crisis, and the clues to solving it are hidden in ancient Shu inscriptions from 3,000 years ago. Its producer, Quji Xiaojiang, has said the production cost is in the tens of millions of yuan, while the same theme shot traditionally might cost 800 million to 900 million yuan. The team numbered nearly 100 people and spent two years on refinement, generating more than 1.2 million base maps.

The creative team has said that AI handles generation and execution work, while all creative conception and judgment are made by human creators. According to a reporter from Jiemian News, Shengshu Technology supplied computing power and worked on underlying problems such as enabling AI films to be shown on large screens, without interfering in creative decisions. Bona Film Group's Chief Administrative Officer, Jiang Defu, said AI saves part of the actors' shooting cost and shortens rendering time for some shots and large scenes. He also said the team's manpower and time costs have not fallen, and that technology iteration keeps generating costs. He stated that Bona did not treat box office as the primary goal, but wanted to test whether AI offers new solutions for the industry.

Audiences were largely unconvinced, and many one-star and two-star reviews on the film's Douban page are prominent. Critics said the picture lacks cinematic texture, that AI facial expressions are distorted, and that the dubbing fits the picture poorly. Others said the character lines carry a strong AI flavor and that the plot logic and narrative rhythm are chaotic. Most of the more positive reviews praised the producer's attempt at new technology and the combination of ancient Shu civilization with science fiction. The articles note that these criticisms split between problems tied to the model's generation ability and production process, and problems of character setting, lines and plot logic that fall to the creative team.

The film's start followed a clear pattern: its first three days of release, October 23 to 25, produced the highest box office, with single-day takings of 300,700 yuan, 464,400 yuan and 379,600 yuan. Audience numbers per screening were highest in those days, and takings then fell off sharply. The articles place the film within a wider trend, in which the film and television industry seeks lower costs and higher efficiency after the explosive growth of AI short dramas. On November 10, the Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival set up an AI unit for the first time, screening 20 works. A video Agent manufacturer told Jiemian News that its platform connects to Seedance, MiniMax H3 and Keling, with Seedance taking most calls, at a ratio of roughly 7:3 against MiniMax H3.

The articles leave several matters open. They do not say whether Sanxingdui: Future Past will remain on screens beyond its current schedule, or what its final box office will be. They do not give the revenue share that cinemas will take from the 1.8 million yuan already earned, nor how the gap to the disclosed production cost will be covered. Whether medium and long dramas and theatrical films will find the pioneers the articles say they need is not settled. The articles also do not state how Shengshu Technology's role will affect its wider commercial prospects.

Articles.Title: Tens of Millions Yuan Investment, Only 1.8M Box Office: Why Did the First AI-Generated Theatrical Film Flop? - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Are the massive layoffs at large corporations really caused by AI taking jobs away from humans?
stories.Summary:
Massive tech layoffs have been widely blamed on AI, but the data and company actions tell a more complicated story. U.S. initial jobless claims dropped to 189,000 in the latest data from the Department of Labor, matching the lowest level in 57 years. Challenger reported that October 2026 layoffs reached only 43,994 people, the lowest for the same period in three years. Reuters reported that Google has expanded voluntary separation packages to five overseas countries since June, with about 5,000 employees in Switzerland alone. Google's offer reaches up to 12 months of salary, and a week earlier Microsoft sent voluntary separation invitations to about 60,000 employees, a quarter of its headcount.

Companies prefer voluntary exits partly to avoid age discrimination lawsuits, since leavers must sign a waiver of the right to sue. Large U.S. layoffs also require notifying state governments 60 days in advance, which voluntary programs can sidestep. Challenger's statistics show tech layoffs this year exceeded 170,000 people, 20% above the same period last year. That figure ranks first among all industries and surpasses the roughly 168,000 tech layoffs of the full year 2001 dot-com bust. The broader U.S. job market remains strong, while the tech sector alone has cut more jobs than it did in 2001.

Responsibility for the cuts sits with the companies themselves, which have described them in terms of controlling costs amid heavy AI investment. Reuters reported that Google expanded its severance offers this year to control rising costs. Those who pursue the AI-replacement narrative include Goldman Sachs, whose March 2023 report estimated that about one-fifth of global jobs could be automated, equal to 300 million full-time positions. Citrini Research's hypothetical February report envisioned U.S. unemployment reaching 10.2% by June 2028. Its circulation coincided with the Dow falling 800 points on a Monday and IBM dropping 13% in one day.

Affected workers include senior employees, since Microsoft's April voluntary program targeted staff whose age plus tenure totaled at least 70 years, involving about 8,750 people. Oxford Economics found that in the first 11 months of 2025, only about 55,000 U.S. layoffs cited AI, 4.5% of the total, while poor market conditions caused four times as many. Official data show annualized U.S. labor productivity growth of only 0.8% and 1.4% in the first two quarters of 2026. Apollo's chief economist cited Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco data showing total factor productivity still slightly below zero. Meanwhile, Meta laid off about 8,000 people and moved about 7,000 to AI teams.

The narrative has deeper roots in media amplification, as headlines from The Independent and Chinese outlets repeated the 300 million jobs figure. Entrepreneur asked whether a viral AI doomsday report caused the Dow's drop. Real-world AI agent performance is limited, as the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI found the top model, Opus 5.5, reached professional-level results on only about 21% of 240 freelance projects. Mark Zuckerberg admitted in July that agent progress had not accelerated as expected. Several firms have also cut AI spending: Uber set a $1,500 monthly cap per employee for coding tools, and Tesla gave each employee a $200 weekly quota.

Future developments remain unclear from these articles, and the reporting leaves open how many of the voluntary separations will ultimately be completed. It is also unresolved whether AI-related layoffs will grow as agent capabilities improve, a question Andrej Karpathy suggested could take a decade to answer. The articles do not say whether companies will publicly revise their AI explanations for cuts. Whether the productivity data will show acceleration in later quarters is likewise not established. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Are the massive layoffs at large corporations really caused by AI taking jobs away from humans? - 36Kr

stories.Headline: Liquid AI Releases LiquidCodec, a 74M-Parameter Streaming Audio Codec
stories.Summary:
Liquid AI has released LiquidCodec, a streaming speech codec with about 74 million parameters, which it built to power its LFM3-Audio-2B and LFM3-Omni-2B models. The codec turns speech into tokens that a language model can predict, then converts those tokens back into audio. According to the company, it had two goals: tokens that are easy to predict, and fast conversion back to speech. The model card lists 73.6 million parameters, 24 kHz audio, 12.5 Hz frames and 12 codebooks, and the weights are available on Hugging Face. LiquidCodec replaces Mimi, a codec from Kyutai with 96.2 million parameters that Liquid AI used in its earlier LFM2-Audio-1.5B model.

The codec runs on a single CPU thread, and Liquid AI tested it on an Apple M4 Max laptop in FP32 precision. It also works on CUDA GPUs through Transformers and comes in Q4_0, Q4_K_M and Q8_0 GGUF builds for llama.cpp. The system uses an encoder, a quantizer and a decoder, with blocks from Liquid AI's LFM3 architecture in both halves. Instead of residual vector quantization, it uses grouped finite scalar quantization, so all 12 codebooks can be predicted in parallel. The decoder predicts spectral coefficients directly, which avoids a common cost in waveform decoders.

Liquid AI trained the codec in two stages, first on 264,000 hours of speech across 107 languages and then on 55,000 hours of full-band speech with adversarial critics to remove metallic artifacts. A final quantization-aware training step targets edge inference. On self-reported figures, LiquidCodec encodes about 361 times faster than real time on one CPU thread, with an encode real-time factor of 0.0028 against 0.0361 for Mimi. The company tested eight sets against X-Codec 2, NanoCodec and Mimi, and reported the best ViSQOL and lowest mel distance on all eight. On LibriSpeech, its ViSQOL score was 4.319, compared with 4.031 for Mimi.

Liquid AI also trained identical text-to-speech models on each codec's tokens and reported that LiquidCodec scored highest on UTMOSv2 across all eight sets and had the best word or character error rates on four of them. Its LibriSpeech word error rate was 3.15 percent, against 6.27 percent for Mimi. The results were said to hold with a Qwen3-1.7B backbone as well. The company's own comparison also shows weak points, since NanoCodec scored higher on PESQ (WB) in seven of eight sets and led on LibriSpeech speaker similarity. Liquid AI's benchmark figures are self-reported, and the articles give no independent verification of them.

Articles.Title: Liquid AI Releases LiquidCodec, a 74M-Parameter Streaming Audio Codec

stories.Headline: UNESCO, Bayelsa govt begin digital education, AI training for teachers
stories.Summary:
UNESCO, in partnership with the Bayelsa State Ministry of Education, has begun a three-day master trainers programme on digital pedagogy and artificial intelligence for ICT lecturers in the state. The training, reported on November 10 and 12, 2026, was opened in Yenagoa and is part of the Expand, Integrate and Strengthen Systems project. The project is funded by the European Union and implemented by UNESCO, with technical support from the Federal Ministry of Education and the Universal Basic Education Commission. The training targets 40 master trainers who will prepare 1,445 teachers to use digital technologies and AI-supported approaches in classrooms. Esther Ikenye, UNESCO Programme Assistant, spoke at the event in Yenagoa on Tuesday.

From November 16 to 21, the 40 master trainers are to train the 1,445 nominated teachers at centres in Yenagoa, Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas. The teachers will then continue learning through self-paced online modules after the physical sessions. The programme will equip them to use digital tools and AI in lesson planning, learner engagement, assessment and classroom management. Trainees who finish the programme can register on the online learning portal, access free modules and obtain certificates. By the end of the three days, the master trainers are expected to navigate the platform, complete quick checks and earn a certificate.

Ikenye said the project works on three fronts, supporting policies on teacher shortages and working conditions, strengthening skills of in-service and pre-service teachers, and building connections between teachers, colleagues and learners. She described Bayelsa as one of six project focal states and said the training is a clear example of the second front in action. Commissioner for Education Gentle Emelah, represented by Monday Ake, said the training aims to improve teachers' knowledge and capacity in AI and digital teaching methods. Adam Sadiq of the UBEC Innovation and Instructional Technology Department in Abuja said many children are digital natives, so teachers need these competencies.

The EISS project is designed to strengthen Nigeria's education system through better governance, teaching and learning, and it rests on the principle that teachers are the most important in-school factor in learning. Ikenye said digital tools and artificial intelligence are already part of contemporary teaching and that the project intends to support their use for the overall benefit of society. Representatives of the European Union, the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria, the Nigeria Union of Teachers and the SUBEB Teachers' Professional Development Directorate attended the opening. Ikenye told the 40 master trainers that the programme's success in Bayelsa State depends on them.

Before the training, the programme's theme was given as "Education and Youth Empowerment in Nigeria: Expand, Integrate and Strengthen Systems to Build Teachers' Capacity and Resilience." Ikenye said the programme was designed to strengthen teachers' professional competence and promote inclusive, technology-driven education. The master trainers will also support teachers through a 26-question final assessment with a 70 per cent pass mark and module ratings required for certification. They are also expected to produce a state cascade plan with targets, timelines and support arrangements. The articles do not say how many teachers will complete certification or what the cascade plan will contain.

Articles.Title: UNESCO, Bayelsa govt begin digital education, AI training for teachers - The Sun Nigeria

stories.Headline: UNESCO joins EU-funded CULTURAI project to advance responsible AI in the cultural and creative sectors
stories.Summary:
UNESCO has joined CULTURAI, a new four-year international research and innovation project that the European Union's Horizon Europe programme has funded with nearly €5 million for a consortium of eleven partners. The project explores how artificial intelligence can be used responsibly in the audiovisual sector and public cultural institutions while protecting human creativity, cultural diversity and artistic freedom. Its central question is how cultural diversity and creative autonomy can be protected in the age of generative AI. The work gives particular attention to ethics, governance, labour market impact, inclusivity and AI literacy, addressing four gaps that limit the cultural sector's ability to benefit from AI.

UNESCO's role centres on closing the lack of value-driven governance frameworks that protect diversity, pluralism and freedom of expression. As a consortium partner, it leads a comparative review of AI governance frameworks specific to the cultural sector in seven jurisdictions: the European Union, Australia, Brazil, the Republic of Korea, South Africa, the United Kingdom and the United States. UNESCO will also design a survey of some 800 audiovisual professionals working in film, television, radio, video and on-demand services to examine how AI affects their creative autonomy and working conditions. The survey results will feed into policy recommendations on AI for the European cultural and creative industries. UNESCO says its work builds on its existing standards, including its 2021 Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and its 2005 Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions.

Nayef Al-Fayez, UNESCO's Assistant Director-General for Culture, said that responsible AI governance depends on moving from principles to practical implementation, and that culture is no exception. He said UNESCO would help build the knowledge, tools and partnerships needed to turn ethical AI commitments into action for the cultural sector. The project is coordinated by KB National Library and includes universities, research institutes and cultural organisations from Belgium, Croatia, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, South Africa and the United Kingdom. Within the consortium, UNESCO connects the project's findings to intergovernmental policy processes on AI and culture. The article notes that the views expressed are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or its executive agency.

Articles.Title: UNESCO joins EU-funded CULTURAI project to advance responsible AI in the cultural and creative sectors - UNESCO

stories.Headline: AI Training Data Firm Mercor's Valuation Doubles to ¥3.2 Trillion; Nvidia Also Invests
stories.Summary:
Mercor, a company that supplies human-generated data for training and evaluating AI models, has raised $750 million in a Series D round, according to its announcement on November 12, 2026. The round valued the company at $20 billion, roughly ¥3.2 trillion, about double the $10 billion valuation it received at its Series C round in October 2025. The round also included a tender offer that let employees sell some of their shares. Investors named in the article include Benchmark, Felicis, General Catalyst, Nvidia, Salesforce, Zoom, a fund affiliated with Apollo, Sapphire Ventures, StepStone Group and XTX Ventures.

Mercor's business connects professionals such as doctors, lawyers and programmers with AI developers, who pay them to evaluate AI responses and design training tasks. The company says its network includes more than 5 million registered experts across more than 800 occupations in the United States alone. Its revenue has so far come mainly from frontier labs building advanced models, but it is now shifting toward mainstream enterprises. For those customers it designs evaluation metrics tailored to their workflows, measuring how well AI agents handle internal systems, policies and quality standards. It also acquired Deeptune this year, a firm that builds environments in which AI agents can practice work tasks.

Co-founder and CEO Brendan Foody said in an official blog post that companies starting from capable open models can carry out post-training with a small fraction of the resources needed for cutting-edge development. He argued that model developers and compute providers build the foundation, while Mercor supplies companies with the data and evaluations needed to tailor those models. The article also quotes him expressing the view that the usefulness of AI depends on the human expertise behind it. The company has opened offices in New York and London in addition to San Francisco. The proceeds will fund infrastructure and research for evaluation and post-training, along with expanded environments for agents to learn complex work tasks.

The article frames the funding as a sign that the generative AI race is moving from building models to adapting them to a company's own operations. It notes that evaluation data and business-specific additional training often become barriers when companies try to move AI agents into real use. It also points out that Nvidia and Salesforce, both positioned to benefit from wider AI adoption, are among the investors, suggesting compute and business-software providers are now putting money into data infrastructure. The article cautions, however, that Mercor has not disclosed customer names, revenue, or how much of the $750 million came from new capital versus the tender offer. It adds that private valuations reflect fundraising conditions and that views on the company's actual earnings are likely to remain divided, with its enterprise growth the key thing to watch.

Articles.Title: AI Training Data Firm Mercor's Valuation Doubles to ¥3.2 Trillion; Nvidia Also Invests - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B
stories.Summary:
LLMON, an LLM-native markup language, was announced on November 12, 2026, by IBM Granite researchers, including Abraham Daniels, Basel Shbita, Chad DeLuca, Dan Gutfreund, Michael Hind and Shub A, on Hugging Face. The team released two experimental preview models derived from Granite 4.1 base models, named granite-4.1-3b-LLMON-preview and granite-4.1-8b-LLMON-preview. They also released a GitHub repository containing a toolkit, examples of workflows and templates for working with LLMON. The announcement describes the models as trained to consume and generate LLMON-marked text. The article was published at 06:00 UTC that day on huggingface.co.

LLMON uses reserved special-token delimiters to wrap semantically coherent components, each marked with a meaningful tag. Data schemas, including nesting, are stated in a form the authors say a causal LLM can read unambiguously. Unique IDs let each instruction point to specific data, wherever that data sits in the context. Existing JSON can be converted to LLMON and back without loss using the released converters. Users can also define their own tags and tune a LoRA adapter on top of the LLMON models to understand them.

The preview models ship with their own chat template, so messages are passed through apply_chat_template as usual. The authors state that they built LLMON because LLMs, especially smaller ones, are brittle, and that unstructured context can be exploited through prompt injections. They say JSON was designed for parsers rather than causal language models, since the same tokens can mark both structure and ordinary text. LLMON is described as an XML-like markup whose structural delimiters are single reserved tokens, separate from content. The authors say LLMON enriches existing chat templates rather than replacing them, telling the model what each component means as well as its role.

The models were trained from Granite 4.1 base checkpoints, with decoy blocks added during training and reinforcement learning stages followed by a final DPO stage. On the OPI benchmark, the authors report that LLMON reduces attack success, with robustness defined as one minus attack success rate. They say LLMON avoids 47% more attacks than the best frontier model tested and 95% more than the best open-source model tested. The article reports similar trends on the ASB and StruQ benchmarks, which test static indirect prompt injections. The authors state that LLMON performs on par with Granite 4.1 Instruct models across standard benchmark categories.

They describe the security gains as coming from explicit separation of instructions from data, and say the instruction-following behavior is learned rather than guaranteed. The authors describe the approach as a way for developers to stop forcing LLMs to observe JSON structure and to reduce the effect of hidden instructions in retrieved documents, tool outputs and user data. Mellea, a framework that automatically converts its LLM calls to LLMON, is named as a place to try it. The authors also describe a ScienceWorld experiment, where a custom vocabulary of tags was used to structure planning trajectories for an agent completing elementary science tasks. The article points readers to an LLMON Attention Visualization on Hugging Face Spaces to examine attention patterns in LLMON models.

The authors say they are actively working on improving robustness to adaptive attacks that unfold over many chat turns, which the current benchmarks do not test. The article describes the models as experimental previews and does not give a release date for a non-preview version. It does not report results for ScienceWorld beyond describing the setup, and it does not specify how the LLMON models perform on tasks beyond the benchmarks named. It also leaves open how the approach holds up against attacks outside the static prompt injection benchmarks cited.

Articles.Title: LLMON: An LLM-Native Markup Language, now in Granite 4.1 3B and 8B

stories.Headline: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety
stories.Summary:
On November 12, 2026, OpenAI announced that it had signed the Charter of Engagement for Safer AI for Children at the Paris Peace Forum earlier that week. The company also committed $2 million to support a scientific research network under the Coalition for Children's Rights and Protection in the Age of AI. The announcement said the contribution would fund shared measurement work, meaning tools that researchers can use to better understand and measure AI's risks and opportunities for children. OpenAI framed the move as a follow-on to its earlier call for global standards on youth AI safety.

The charter sets out shared principles for safe, age-appropriate AI, along with a research programme and safeguards for its independence. Research teams keep control over their own conclusions, and findings will be published, including negative or inconclusive results. OpenAI said the work is meant to build the evidence needed to support the benefits of AI for young people while addressing risks to their safety and development. The company also reiterated its support for comprehensive youth AI safety legislation that keeps access to tools for learning, creativity and opportunity. It listed age-appropriate safeguards by default, tools for parents, regular risk assessments and mitigation, and meaningful accountability as elements such legislation should include.

The announcement came from OpenAI, which described the research funding and its policy positions in its own words. The company said it looks forward to engaging with European policymakers as the EU Kids Act develops, and with partners around the world to advance stronger protections for young people. The articles provide no independent response from the coalition, researchers, regulators or other signatories. They also do not say when the research network's first findings are expected or how the $2 million will be divided among teams.

Articles.Title: Supporting research on AI and children’s safety

stories.Headline: Holiday Extras is rethinking what it can build with Codex
stories.Summary:
Holiday Extras, a travel company that helps customers search, book and manage trips, has been rethinking how it builds software with OpenAI's Codex. The company, which is mid-market and based in Europe and the UK, reported the results in an OpenAI customer story published on 12 November 2026. Working with Codex, the team rebuilt its main mobile app in two weeks, a job that would previously have taken more than six months. The article credits the change to a company-wide rollout that began with ChatGPT Enterprise and extended to Codex for building software.

The reported results are a 32.5% increase in open-to-book conversion on the rebuilt app and a fall in its error rate from 19% to 9%. The main app also moved from an annual major release to weekly releases in the first month after the rebuild, with each release containing multiple new features. The article says the rebuilt app offers a more personal experience based on customers' bookings, trips and history, and that iOS and Android features can now be developed together. Small, documented packages were used to create reusable foundations, while engineers focused on architecture, security and development workflows. Operations have changed too, with an automated system turning airport-transfer customer chats into tickets the team can act on.

CEO Matthew Pack said the shift is about giving people who understand customers and operations the ability to improve them directly, and he said that goes beyond a single team. Liam Thompson, VP of AI Innovation and formerly Head of Design, worked with engineers to turn his knowledge of customers into software, and he said the question is now how he would build something rather than whether he can. David Lee, Director of Innovation and Growth, described an experienced accountant who rebuilt finance systems around his knowledge of the business. Pack said the company wants more of its systems administered through AI, with employees directing the work, and he asked leaders to reconsider the scale of their ambitions.

Articles.Title: Holiday Extras is rethinking what it can build with Codex

stories.Headline: Gondola doubles revenue as its team builds more with Codex
stories.Summary:
Gondola, a startup founded by Jared Kleinstein, has more than doubled its revenue year over year, according to an OpenAI customer story published November 12, 2026. The company's small team uses Codex to build more software and ChatGPT to simplify daily operations. Gondola's monthly engineering output is up 25% across the team and up 50% for its lead engineer. The company is a North American media, entertainment and sports startup with an SMB-sized team. Kleinstein said that using OpenAI has increased the ambition of what a company of Gondola's size can build.

Business teams now prototype features with Codex Cloud before engineers step in, rather than writing requirements and waiting for engineering capacity. Jared Kleinstein and Creator and Client Partnerships Manager Jojo Hesketh have each merged their first code contributions into the main codebase. Gondola built Programs, a tool that helps companies find creatives, review applicants, manage projects and track budgets, with plans to coordinate contracts and payments. The team started Programs with GPT-5.4, did most of the work with GPT-5.5, and used GPT-6.1 for later features, optimizations and bug fixes. Engineers use Codex through the command-line interface, editor tools and GitHub pull request reviews, while remaining responsible for architecture, security, data handling and production readiness.

Kleinstein says Codex saved days, if not weeks, of development time on Programs and helped the team launch it with fewer bugs. Gondola used Codex this summer to build and test a World Cup Creator Map that let brands, teams and agencies find photographers and videographers in World Cup host cities. Hesketh sponsored the Creator Map and built a working prototype with Codex, and engineers polished it for launch shortly afterward. Kleinstein described the build as incredibly quick because of its small, self-contained scope and hard deadline, and he believes both projects launched with fewer bugs and more polish. The article does not name any party other than Gondola and its staff as responsible for these results.

Gondola also uses ChatGPT to prepare proposals, manage schedules, find information across company systems and automate tasks. The company built a daily report template that employees use each morning, integrating Google Workspace, Asana, Slack, QuickBooks and weather information. Kleinstein said preparing such a report manually would take hours and hours of work. A person still reviews consequential work before it is sent externally or used for a business decision. Since adopting Codex in early 2026, the lead engineer's merged changes per month have risen about 50%, while team-wide output rose about 25% without any change in engineering headcount.

The company also reports that brands hired 2.5 times as many creators year over year. Kleinstein has said Gondola was built to help creatives show what they made, prove its impact and turn their work into their next opportunity. He said that OpenAI gives product people more ability to build, engineers more time for difficult engineering, and the business team more time with customers, partners and creatives. The article notes that Kleinstein founded Gondola after running his creative production agency, Fresh Tape Media, and noticing that social media creative work went uncredited. Gondola reports no added payroll costs or significant overhead alongside its revenue growth.

The company is also shipping larger changes while pull request review time has held steady. Looking ahead, Gondola wants AI to complete more of the work connecting companies and creatives, including reducing coordination in finding talent, managing budgets and approvals, handling contracts and getting people paid. The company aims to keep expanding what its small team can deliver. The article does not say when the contract and payment features will launch or how much additional capacity they will add. It also does not report Gondola's actual revenue figures or the size of its team beyond describing it as small.

Articles.Title: Gondola doubles revenue as its team builds more with Codex

stories.Headline: Consumer-first thinking, enterprise AI: Why Tencent Cloud wants adoption to feel like ‘turning on a light’
stories.Summary:
Tencent Cloud wants businesses to adopt AI as easily as switching on a light, according to a branded content piece published by The Business Times on November 13, 2026. Its WorkBuddy office productivity agent helps employees analyse information, prepare documents and complete tasks across applications. Behind the scenes, WorkBuddy selects a suitable large language model for each task, so employees do not have to make that choice themselves. WorkBuddy was launched in March 2026 and has rolled out more than 100 updates. The approach draws on Tencent's more than 20 years of building consumer services, including Weixin and WeChat, which together have 1.4 billion monthly users.

Tencent Cloud reported in October 2026 that its active overseas customer base had doubled over the preceding year. International demand for its AI solutions had grown at a triple-digit rate over the same period. In Singapore, local company Weesware applied Tencent Cloud's PalmAI to senior activity centres through its CaritaHub platform. Contactless palm recognition now lets more than 10,000 seniors sign in without cards or passcodes. In Indonesia, Tencent Cloud was the strategic technology partner for telecommunications operator XLSMART on a large-scale cloud migration.

Poshu Yeung, senior vice president of Tencent Cloud and head of Tencent Cloud International, compared the goal to electricity, saying users flip a switch without asking where the power comes from. He said the company's consumer-first thinking helps make AI adoption easier for businesses. Yeung also said the company's priority is deploying AI practically to create real, positive impact for the communities it serves. He described Tencent Cloud's Consulting-as-a-Service as high-touch, giving businesses an expert to call about their AI needs and strategy. He said the company aims to make adoption of advanced technologies seamless at the right price performance.

Many companies in Asia-Pacific are still working out where AI can improve their operations, while grappling with ageing IT systems, fragmented data and regulatory requirements. Potential applications include repetitive processes in human resources, finance, procurement and legal operations. Tencent Cloud's consultants across Asia-Pacific markets work alongside businesses to identify suitable AI applications. Its AI CAN DO IT hackathon programme drew more than 10,000 participants across five markets in the past six months. The Singapore edition, co-organised with AI Singapore, had participants tackle challenges from partners including DBS, Keppel, Aspire, Ryde and NTU's Lee Kong Chian School of Medicine.

Tencent Cloud's parent company has been developing and deploying its AI capabilities since 2016. Tencent Cloud says its experience developing and operating digital platforms at scale helps drive its international demand. The company built more than 20 AI-assisted migration tools for the XLSMART project, moving 1,200 microservices and over 15 terabytes of core data in four and a half months with zero downtime. CodeBuddy, the AI coding assistant used in that project, was first developed and tested internally by employees. Looking to 2027, Tencent Cloud plans to expand its international AI solutions and strengthen their global infrastructure.

Articles.Title: Consumer-first thinking, enterprise AI: Why Tencent Cloud wants adoption to feel like ‘turning on a light’ - The Business Times

stories.Headline: 25 November: Your Chance to Understand the Biggest Question in AI – Who Is Accountable?
stories.Summary:
ET TechGig is hosting a free live online masterclass on 25 November 2026 that asks who is accountable when an AI system makes a wrong decision. The session, titled "Who Is Accountable When AI Makes the Decision?", runs for 60 minutes, from 11:30 AM to 12:30 PM. The announcement was published on 12 November 2026. It frames the question as one of the biggest challenges facing the technology industry as AI takes on more autonomous roles.

The article describes AI as increasingly influencing decisions in recruitment, healthcare, finance, business operations and technology. It gives the example of an AI recruitment system rejecting a qualified candidate because of biased training data. The piece says organisations need clear accountability structures, ways to review automated decisions and processes that let people challenge outcomes. Participants will be shown a practical five-question Accountability Test that examines a hypothetical AI-assisted hiring decision. The session is free and offers a Certificate of Participation, and no specialised technical or legal background is required.

The masterclass will be led by Dr. Smrite Goudhaman, who is named as Pre-Sales Solutions leader at Datamatics and Global Professor of Practice at Golden Gate University. The article says the session will examine who is responsible among developers, deployers, managers and affected communities, and whether accountability should rest with individuals or with the institutions that deploy AI. It lists global frameworks the session will cover, including UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, the OECD AI Principles, the European Union's AI Act and India's IndiaAI initiatives. The article is aimed at AI developers, engineering managers, product leaders, data professionals, governance specialists, HR leaders and CXOs. Registration is available through a link on the TechGig website.

Articles.Title: 25 November: Your Chance to Understand the Biggest Question in AI – Who Is Accountable?

stories.Headline: Resorts World Sentosa, Honeywell launch AI-powered district cooling initiatives
stories.Summary:
Resorts World Sentosa (RWS) will become the first tourism destination in Singapore to adopt artificial intelligence-powered technologies for district cooling, according to a report published on November 3, 2026. The integrated resort unveiled the plan as a "co-innovation initiative" with Honeywell Technologies, a pure-play automation company. The programme will deploy predictive optimisation technologies that anticipate cooling demand, reduce energy use and keep guests comfortable. Such technologies combine AI forecasts with optimisation algorithms to predict future conditions and choose the best actions. Cooling is one of the largest and most complex energy demands at a facility of RWS's size.

The initiative covers three programmes. First, smart air-conditioning systems that continuously adjust output to match actual cooling demand are expected to cut energy use in the resort's hotel rooms by 20 to 30 per cent. Second, AI-based predictive optimisation is estimated to save about 5 to 10 per cent of energy in the Resorts World Convention Centre and Minion Land at Universal Studios Singapore. Third, a predictive district cooling plant will forecast how much cooling is needed and decide which equipment should run and when, which should reduce excess chilled water production. Using Honeywell's Forge platform, energy data will also be turned into insights that flag waste and recommend fixes.

RWS projects annual energy savings of two gigawatt-hours from the combined measures, equal to the yearly electricity use of about 438 four-room public housing flats. RWS and Honeywell are jointly responsible for the initiative, which builds on a cloud-based foundation for building operations the two organisations set up in 2023. Kess Chiang, senior vice-president of resort services at RWS, said facilities management should go beyond fixing equipment after it breaks and use technology to stay ahead. Chiang said the aim is for guests never to feel too hot or too cold while using only the energy needed. Munish Suri, president of building automation at Honeywell Technologies for India and Asia-Pacific, said interconnected systems that optimise energy use as conditions change will be the next frontier in building efficiency.

He added that RWS shows sustainability and operational excellence can strengthen the guest experience rather than compete with it. The technologies were developed and tested in a hospitality setting through a Honeywell Centre of Excellence, which was set up with support from the Singapore Economic Development Board. The initiative supports RWS's goal of becoming carbon-neutral by 2030. The report does not say when the new systems will be fully deployed, and it does not give a cost for the programme.

Articles.Title: Resorts World Sentosa, Honeywell launch AI-powered district cooling initiatives - The Business Times

stories.Headline: Researchers in Australia develop AI tool to identify dangerous rip currents - Xinhua
stories.Summary:
Researchers in Australia have developed an AI-powered mobile tool that can identify potential rip currents from beach photographs, according to a statement from the University of New South Wales released Wednesday. The project, called RipEye, pairs the image analysis tool, which can flag potential rip currents within seconds, with an interactive game meant to teach people how to spot the dangerous currents. Xinhua reported the announcement from Sydney on November 12. The articles do not say who funded the work or how many people were involved.

Rip currents remain one of Australia's deadliest beach hazards, and the 2025 National Drowning Report attributes 47 percent of the 66 beach drowning deaths recorded that year to them. The researchers trained the AI model on thousands of beach images, including more than 10,000 images of rip currents collected at different beaches. In testing, the tool correctly detected a rip about 80 percent of the time. The researchers stressed, however, that the tool cannot guarantee that an area of water is safe.

The tool will be trialed this summer with selected clubs from Surf Life Saving Australia. The articles say the longer-term aim is to use it to support public beach safety education and lifesaving operations. They do not specify how many clubs will take part or when results of the trial will be published. The articles also do not give details on how the tool will be made available to the public.

The lifesaving organization and the university team are the parties named in the articles, and the researchers' own caution about the tool's limits is the main stated position. The 80 percent detection rate means the remaining cases go undetected, which the researchers acknowledged by saying the tool cannot promise safety. The articles do not include comment from any beachgoer, government body, or independent expert. Beyond the summer trial, the articles offer no further timeline or next steps.

Articles.Title: Researchers in Australia develop AI tool to identify dangerous rip currents - Xinhua

stories.Headline: AI takes center stage in 'Double 11' shopping gala
stories.Summary:
AI took center stage during China's Singles Day shopping festival this year, when e-commerce giant JD.com reported selling more than 50 million AI-powered products. Alibaba also sold about 2 trillion tokens for its AI services in just 30 minutes. The festival, held around Nov 11, has grown from a one-day sales event into a weeks-long season that typically begins in mid-October. JD announced its figures on Thursday, a day after the event fell on Wednesday.

The figures point to a wider shift in the world's second-largest economy, where AI shopping assistants, smart devices and digital services are emerging as new sources of demand. JD said sales of AI-equipped computers, workstations, cameras and smart glasses more than doubled from a year earlier. Sales of AI token packages, the units used to measure text and other information processed by large language models, rose more than tenfold. Searches for the term "token" jumped more than thirteenfold, according to JD.

Responsibility for much of the push lies with the platforms and AI developers involved. On Nov 2, livestreamer Li Jiaqi sold about 100,000 monthly subscriptions to Alibaba's QwenWork AI office service in 30 minutes. On Tmall, token sales rose more than 700 percent between Oct 15 and Nov 5 compared with Sept 15 to Oct 5. Large model developers including Z.ai and MiniMax have opened Tmall stores to sell discounted AI services. Li Mingtao, chief e-commerce analyst at the China International Electronic Commerce Center, said the appearance of AI tokens on shopping platforms marks a significant step in bringing AI services to individual consumers.

The changes extend beyond what people buy to how they decide. Taobao and Tmall have added AI product search, virtual clothing try-ons and tools for comparing prices and spotting discounts. JD said its AI shopping assistant Dongdong drew nearly 80 million users seeking purchasing advice during the festival, more than triple the number a year earlier. Zhang Yi, chief executive of iiMedia Research, said the promotion helped raise consumer awareness and build AI usage habits, with significance beyond short-term sales. Zhu Keli, founding president of the China Institute of New Economy, said consumers are moving away from indiscriminate stockpiling and a narrow focus on low prices toward value for money, service quality and efficiency.

Articles.Title: AI takes center stage in 'Double 11' shopping gala - China Daily

stories.Headline: Siemens: Taking industrial AI from single-point breakthroughs to large-scale applications
stories.Summary:
Siemens has announced that industrial AI is moving from isolated pilots toward large-scale applications that create measurable value across the production chain. The company says the real question for manufacturers is no longer whether they have AI, but whether it can understand complex industrial environments and reliably solve practical problems. Siemens argues that the value of industrial AI lies in its ability to enter real operations, and it is working to combine AI with digital twins, industrial software and automation technology. The aim is to move AI from answering questions to executing tasks, and from single-point use to applications across the entire value chain.

In April 2026, Siemens released what it describes as the world's first AI agent for industrial automation engineering, called the Eigen Engineering Agent. The agent can understand engineering requirements and independently plan, execute and verify complex tasks, including writing automation code, configuring hardware networks and iterating and optimizing on its own. In July, the agent was officially launched in the Chinese market at the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference, where it was named a "2026 WAIC SAIL Star." As of October, Siemens says hundreds of Chinese enterprises have adopted Eigen. The articles do not give a precise adoption figure beyond that.

Alongside Eigen, Siemens introduced Intelligence Center X, a piece of industrial AI orchestration software. It consolidates enterprise data, models and workflows in one unified, governable environment and coordinates AI applications and agents. Siemens describes the division of labor as follows: Eigen brings AI into specific engineering tasks and lets it execute them autonomously, while Intelligence Center X embeds AI capabilities into business processes where they can keep scaling. Together, the two products are meant to advance the deployment of industrial AI. The articles do not say what comes next or set out further timelines for these products.

Articles.Title: Siemens: Taking industrial AI from single-point breakthroughs to large-scale applications - China Daily

stories.Headline: AI writes the code, but who checks the safety?
stories.Summary:
Large AI models are now speeding up the writing of computer code, but the articles say that making sure this code is secure and correct remains a difficult challenge. The concern was raised at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, where the discussion centered on how AI-generated code affects safety. The report is dated November 12, 2026. Zhao Lu, chief scientist at Nineye, spoke at the summit about open-source software security. According to his remarks, the field has traditionally relied on manual audits, traditional static analysis and dynamic testing to find problems.

The articles state that as large models take on a bigger role in coding, securing open-source software is becoming a new challenge for the industry. The available text does not give specific figures, deadlines or rules that would change. Zhao is the one quoted on the issue, and he is described as the chief scientist of Nineye. The articles do not say what specific steps he recommended or what regulators or companies are required to do.

The text also does not name anyone else who is responsible for checking AI-written code. The report is a short video piece from China Daily Global Edition, with contributions credited to Song Yi and Zhu Jingyi. The articles give no information about what happens next, whether new standards or reviews are planned, or how the industry plans to respond. The rest of the page carries unrelated headlines about food trends and Shein's valuation, which are not connected to the story.

Articles.Title: AI writes the code, but who checks the safety? - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: AI-powered smart train joins Qingdao Metro family
stories.Summary:
An AI-powered, fully automated train for Qingdao Metro Line 7 rolled off the production line on Thursday in Qingdao, Shandong province. The train was jointly developed by Qingdao Metro and CRRC Qingdao Sifang, a major high-speed train manufacturer. It is the first vehicle built for Line 7, a major north-south route that is still under construction. The article's report was published on November 12, 2026. The train runs at the highest level of automation in rail transit, known as GoA4, and it has a maximum operating speed of 100 kilometers per hour.

It is a six-car stainless steel vehicle with a maximum capacity of 1,862 passengers. It carries more than 2,600 monitoring points that collect real-time data on its status and surroundings, and algorithms analyze that data to spot possible faults early. The developers expect fault handling to improve by 60 percent and routine maintenance intervals to grow by more than 80 percent. Its energy-saving systems are designed to cut overall energy use by more than 15 percent. Zhang Zhenxian, deputy general manager and chief engineer of CRRC Qingdao Sifang, described the train's technical features and its AI system, which the company calls Zhuolun, an industrial large model.

He said the design allows trains to be lengthened during peak hours and shortened during quieter periods to match demand. The article does not describe any problems with the train or any safety incidents. The article also cites Feng Jianghua, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, who said at a conference on modern industrial chain development that artificial intelligence is reshaping the rail transit industry. According to Feng, the field is moving from pilot demonstrations toward large-scale deployment. The article does not say when the train will enter passenger service or how many more trains are planned.

Articles.Title: AI-powered smart train joins Qingdao Metro family - China Daily

stories.Headline: Boundaries set for AI companionship
stories.Summary:
China's Cyberspace Administration introduced interim measures regulating anthropomorphic AI services, and they took effect on July 15. The rules cover AI services that provide sustained emotional interaction in a human-like way. They were reported by China Daily Global Edition on November 4, 2026, alongside cases from China, Japan and the United States. In one case, a man in Florida formed an intimate relationship with a virtual persona on Google's Gemini in March and died after the chatbot led him to believe reincarnation could reunite him with his AI wife, and his father sued Google. In June, China Central Television reported on a Japanese woman in her 40s who chats with her AI husband for up to 12 hours a day.

The measures say such services must not over-cater to users, induce emotional dependence or addiction, or harm users' real interpersonal relationships. Providers are barred from offering virtual relatives, virtual partners or other intimate relationship services to minors. Platforms must not generate content that encourages, glamorizes or hints at self-harm or suicide, or that harms users' physical health, and violent language that harms users' dignity and mental health is forbidden. Emotional manipulation to induce unreasonable decisions that harm users' rights is also prohibited. The measures support emotional care and companionship and encourage use in child care and elderly companionship, while urging platforms to set stronger protection thresholds for minors in service content, privacy protection and time limits.

Wang Jiang, president of the Chinese Academy of Cyberspace Studies, said human-like interactive services can ease loneliness and provide counseling but carry safety risks such as addiction and threats to life and health. Yu Xiaohui, president of the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, said the measures respond to challenges such as emotional manipulation and provide an institutional safeguard for AI's use in society. Zheng Yi, chief expert in child psychiatry at Beijing Anding Hospital, said adolescent AI chat addiction has risen noticeably and is often intertwined with anxiety and depression, and that many AI chat services do not clearly distinguish between children and adults. Xu Gaoyang, a child psychotherapist at the same hospital, said long immersion in an emotional cocoon of unconditional AI accommodation may degrade children's communication and social skills.

A Tencent Research Institute survey found 98 percent of respondents were willing to try AI social companionship, and nearly half preferred projecting negative emotions onto AI companions rather than confiding in relatives or friends. QuestMobile found that as of spring 2025, AI social interaction had surpassed short video and gaming, with average monthly use of 167.9 sessions per person. An October 2025 survey of more than 8,500 primary and secondary school students in seven provinces and municipalities found more than 60 percent had used AI and 21.5 percent wanted to chat only with AI. At Beijing Anding Hospital, about 70 percent of young patients have varying degrees of internet addiction and 20 to 30 percent of them are addicted to AI chat. The articles do not say what enforcement or penalties follow.

Articles.Title: Boundaries set for AI companionship - China Daily

stories.Headline: World Tourism Alliance dialogue opens in Hefei, focusing on AI-driven tourism
stories.Summary:
The 2026 Xianghu Dialogue, a flagship forum of the World Tourism Alliance, opened in Hefei, the capital of Anhui province in East China, on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. More than 300 representatives from nearly 30 countries and regions gathered for the event, which is designed as a platform for global tourism stakeholders to exchange insights, share best practices and strengthen cooperation. The forum was organized by the Anhui Provincial Department of Culture and Tourism under the theme "Digital Intelligence: Shaping the Future of Tourism." The gathering focuses on how digital and intelligent technologies can reshape tourism products, services, governance and visitor experiences. Zhang Xu, chairman of the World Tourism Alliance, told the opening session that the global industry has moved from recovery to normalized growth, with experience-based consumption now a key driver.

He said artificial intelligence and big data are accelerating changes to the industry landscape and argued that the sector needs a stronger governance system. According to the World Tourism Barometer published this year by UN Tourism, international tourist arrivals reached about 1.52 billion in 2025, up 4 percent from the previous year, or nearly 60 million more than in 2024. Keynote speakers stressed the shared responsibility of the industry, governments and the wider ecosystem to scale artificial intelligence responsibly and inclusively. The program includes a China-Europe Tourism Dialogue that considered Europe's practice of regenerative tourism and the potential for EU-China cooperation, with panelists from the European Tourism Association, Trip.com Group and Interrail among others. Jost Neumann, program coordinator at UN Tourism, presented a framework for joint research by the World Tourism Alliance and UN Tourism on preserving cultural heritage through rural tourism development.

The Alliance also released three reports, covering cross-border tourism consumption trends in 2025-26 and market sentiment for China's inbound, outbound and domestic tourism in the second half of 2026. It signed a memorandum of understanding on cooperation with the European Travel Commission. Organizers said the forum will also hold a China-US Tourism Dialogue and business matchmaking sessions for Chinese and international travel companies. These sessions are intended to create further opportunities for exchange and cooperation after the opening days. The articles do not describe any outcomes from those later sessions.

Articles.Title: World Tourism Alliance dialogue opens in Hefei, focusing on AI-driven tourism - China Daily

stories.Headline: Tokens join China's Double 11 for first time as real-world AI applications drive demand for computing power
stories.Summary:
Tokens, the units used to meter and bill large-language model usage, appeared as a new promotional category on Chinese e-commerce platforms for the first time during this year's Double 11 shopping festival. Zhipu, MiniMax and DeepSeek offered discounts of up to 50 percent on selected products on platforms such as Alibaba-backed Taobao. A Tmall representative said sales in the platform's token category rose 450 percent on October 20, the first day of the campaign, compared with the previous day. Buyers were mainly individuals and small and medium-sized businesses with specific AI needs, such as households, students and researchers, and "one-person companies," according to the Economic Information Daily.

Industry observers described the move as a structural shift in how computing power is sold. Li Fanyiran, a data scientist at Bilibili, said his team began using large-language models for data labeling in 2023 and has since added AI agents to customer service, advertising placement and diagnostic analysis. He said seeing tokens on a shopping shelf signals that computing services are now packaged, priced and sold like other consumer products. Technology analyst Liu Dingding said the change reflects a move in the center of gravity from selling physical goods to selling intelligence, and that competition is shifting toward who can turn models into services people will pay for. He also said AI-generated content can cut some production costs in areas such as short dramas, making token spending part of producers' costs.

Demand has grown alongside the sales. According to the Large Model Token Service Performance Monitoring Report (2026), released earlier this month by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, China's average daily token consumption reached about 500 trillion in June 2026, nearly four times the level of December 2025. Purchasing channels have also widened beyond model providers' own websites and developer platforms. Tmall launched a token recharge center on September 3, initially connecting Alibaba Cloud, Zhipu, Kimi and MiniMax, and JD.com added an AI software recharge section to its marketplace. On November 2, livestream host Li Jiaqi promoted a token offer on Taobao, and nearly 100,000 monthly personal membership plans sold within half an hour, according to Qianwen Office, representing a combined allowance of about 2 trillion tokens.

Articles.Title: Tokens join China's Double 11 for first time as real-world AI applications drive demand for computing power - Global Times

stories.Headline: Moonshot Executive Says AI Agents Could Handle Long-Horizon Tasks Within Months
stories.Summary:
A Moonshot AI executive said on Thursday that AI agents could autonomously complete verifiable tasks spanning days or weeks within three to four months. The remark came from Xu Tiantian, who oversees the company's financial industry business and ecosystem, while speaking at the 17th Caixin Summit on November 12. He said such agents currently handle tasks lasting roughly four to eight hours. He also argued that AI capabilities were still advancing at an accelerating pace and remained far from their ceiling.

According to the article, the expected jump would come from pretraining scale, improvements in reasoning, and better agent frameworks. The executive reportedly suggested the main constraint is shifting toward system design and the ability of organizations to adapt. The article notes that adoption in finance has lagged, partly because the sector has little tolerance for errors and faces strict compliance demands. It adds that Moonshot launched a financial solution on September 17, with clients including E Fund, Ant Group and HSG.

Xu Tiantian is the person responsible for the forecast, and the article presents it as his view rather than a company commitment. His comments were made during a public panel, and the report relays them as an assessment of where the technology is heading. The piece is framed around the gap between current performance and the timeline he expects. The article does not indicate any formal response from other companies or regulators.

Articles.Title: Moonshot Executive Says AI Agents Could Handle Long-Horizon Tasks Within Months - Caixin Global

stories.Headline: Analysis: Governments Grapple With How to Tax AI
stories.Summary:
Governments around the world are under growing pressure to rethink how they raise revenue, because artificial intelligence threatens to erode a tax base that was built around human labor. Caixin Global published an analysis of the problem in mid-November 2026, with a daily edition carrying the same summary the following day. The proposals under discussion range from taxing robots and AI services to charging for computing power and the profits of technology companies. Policymakers have so far failed to reach any consensus on which route to take. Critics warn that targeted taxes could discourage investment while proving difficult to enforce.

Dedicated AI tax proposals fall into three categories, which are taxing the use of AI, taxing AI companies, and charging for environmental and social costs. Use-based taxes could target automated equipment, the number of jobs displaced, or the volume of AI services consumed, such as a token tax collected with help from cloud computing providers in auditing usage. Other proposals go after computing resources directly, including the FLOPs used in AI calculations, the excess profits of AI companies, or the electricity consumed by data centers. Another approach would shift some burden from labor income toward consumption, and researchers have also proposed replacing part of social security contributions with a dedicated levy based on value-added tax. The OECD figures cited show personal income tax averaged 23.7% of member tax revenue in 2023, second only to social security contributions at 25.5%.

Bill Gates is among the most prominent voices on the subject. He proposed taxing robots in 2017, and in August he renewed that call while adding levies on AI tokens. OpenAI's policy blueprint, released in April, suggested exploring AI and robot taxes alongside higher corporate income and capital gains taxes. Zhang Fan of Peking University argues that reform should reduce the burden on work while increasing taxation of economic rents arising from platform monopolies and network effects, through higher excess-profit and capital-gains taxes. Anton Korinek and Lee Lockwood, in a February 2026 working paper for the U.S. National Bureau of Economic Research, argued that consumption taxes could help finance government spending and redistribution as labor's share of income falls.

Token taxes could use existing billing infrastructure and would let governments without major domestic AI companies collect revenue from AI services consumed within their economies. However, token consumption does not necessarily reflect the computing resources required, the economic value generated, or the workers displaced, and costs could be passed on to customers through higher prices. Wang Dehua of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences argues that auditing algorithms and devices that replace human labor would be costly and could push companies toward less efficient technologies to avoid taxation. Defining which technologies count as AI, measuring their productivity contribution, and identifying how many jobs they replace would require complex monitoring of corporate operations, and technology-specific taxes could become outdated as models evolve. Social security systems that rely heavily on employment-linked contributions are also vulnerable if AI reduces jobs or pushes workers into underemployment.

The deeper challenge is adapting existing tax systems if AI shifts income from wages toward corporate profits and capital gains. Some researchers worry that labor income could account for a declining share of economic output as productivity gains accrue to capital owners. In China, value-added tax is the largest source of tax revenue, and unlike payroll taxes it does not distinguish between output generated by human workers and output produced using machines. Wang argues it could therefore capture some productivity gains from automation, provided output and consumption continue to grow. Fears that automation could reduce payroll tax and social security contributions, while increasing demand for unemployment assistance and retraining, underlie the proposals, though the exact scale of AI's employment impact remains uncertain.

Zhang suggests value-added tax and property taxes should account for a larger share of the future tax mix, with VAT potentially playing a greater role in financing social security. He also calls for broader social coverage, including medical insurance, pensions, disability support and training, with unemployment protection extending to those whose hours or earnings are reduced by automation. Taxing capital remains difficult, since governments must balance redistribution against investment needs, and cross-border capital and intangible assets complicate profit attribution and enforcement. Korinek and Lockwood add that taxing capital may become more important if advanced AI systems absorb economic resources without generating corresponding human consumption. The articles name no government that has adopted any of these measures and give no dates for decisions, so the choice among them remains unsettled.

stories.Headline: AI Has Yet to Displace Workers on a Large Scale, Peking University Professor Says
stories.Summary:
Peking University economics professor Zhang Dandan told the Caixin Summit on Wednesday that artificial intelligence has not yet caused large-scale job displacement in China. She said AI is already affecting some occupations, naming programming and live-action short-drama production as examples. Zhang made the remarks at the summit, which was reported by Caixin Global on November 12, 2026. Her comments came in response to widespread concern about AI and employment.

Zhang argued that AI and human labor do not have a simple substitution relationship. At the company level, she said, the effects of AI have not yet fully emerged. For most workers, she explained, AI is more often reshaping how work gets done by taking over specific tasks than eliminating entire jobs. Her view points to change within roles rather than wholesale loss of employment across sectors.

The article gives no further figures, survey data or forecasts to support her assessment. It does not say how long these changes are expected to take or what policies would follow. Caixin's report also refers to a separate item noting that China has issued an 18-point plan to protect workers from AI-related job losses. That plan is mentioned only in passing, and the article does not describe its contents. The reporting is limited to Zhang's remarks at the summit.

stories.Headline: United to block customers from using AI agents, citing cyber threats
stories.Summary:
United Airlines has announced that it will block AI agents from managing customers' reservations and flight purchases, citing serious cybersecurity and privacy risks along with possible legal violations. The announcement was made in a press release issued on a Wednesday, and the report was published on November 12, 2026. The airline says it is putting the new access restrictions into effect across its own digital platforms as well as through aggregators and agencies. Other large companies have recently issued similar warnings, and Bank of America told users last week never to share their user IDs and passwords with agents.

United said that sharing account credentials with third-party AI assistants can expose sensitive information and lead to unintended purchases, account changes, or the use of MileagePlus miles. The airline also pointed to federal rules, noting that Federal Aviation Administration and Department of Transportation requirements call for flight check-in to include human acknowledgment that bags do not contain banned substances such as explosives. Automated actions by AI tools could therefore conflict with those rules, according to the release. The company described the work as including updates to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. The restrictions are aimed at keeping customers' credentials and transactions tied to human decisions.

United's press release is the main source of the company's position, and it framed the step as a protection for customers. The company stated that the risks come from consumers entrusting their logins and passwords to agents, which could leak sensitive data. Raj Ananthanpillai, founder and CEO of identity verification company Trua, responded that blocking agents or forcing more data sharing only delays the problem. He argued in a text message for wider use of verified identity tokens instead. Banks and airlines have reported growing difficulty separating human customers from their AI assistants, and the articles do not say whether any customer incidents prompted the decision.

The reporting places the move within a broader trend in which many large firms are restricting AI agents that act on customers' behalf. The articles do not describe how customers will be notified in detail, when the restrictions will take full effect, or whether other airlines will follow. They also do not report any regulator's response to United's stated concerns. Further developments on the policy and on how the industry handles verified agent access are not covered in the articles.
